# Chapter Twenty-One: Religious War

“Are we sure this so-called armory still exists, we are talking generations since the church did battle with the mages” Emissary Hutchin said the look of disdain for the tall grass and wooded area evident on his face. He had spent the entire week complaining Nero took a breath calming himself since it would do no good to snap at the emissary “Emisarry, if this armory exists, it would give us a huge advantage when confronting the Empress, this trip is worth it, besides Messenger McCourt is one of the foremost experts on Messenger history, if I trust anyone with knowing the locations of a secret ancient cache of weapon and armor, it would be him” he finished, his tone firm but not angry hopefully the man took the hint the subject was closed.

Nero understood the reservation of the other men, enacting of the agreement was not something done lightly, and he could see the reservations and fear on the men’s faces. After generations of guiding mankind to the path of Aurtus they were taking a real active role in the present politics of a nation. The echoes of this action would be far reaching, and all three men knew it. Nero also knew the importance of a weapons cache from the era of mage wars, the church had been the one to bring the mages to heel.

They had created weapons and armor allowing them to combat mages whose powers were now legendary, if they were to face off against the Empress and her mages, these would be critical. Nero understood the change that was happening even if the emissaries did not yet, the church would become the power within Vicor and in doing so set a precedent, one that would echo throughout the rest of the continent, one that would no longer see the followers of Aurtus dismissed so easily, he was bringing his order back to the table of power. But Nero was not as concerned about that as he was with the Mages, the Mages who had subjugated his people, the Mages who had finally shown their true colors.

The Order of the Dragon may not have been involved but they definitely did not try and stop those they had promised to police, to control so that this would not happen again. Nero saw the failure in the agreement, the church should haver never trusted the mages, never had allowed the mages to create their own order and police themselves. He would change that Nero reflected; he would ensure this type of thing would never happen again.

“I found the entrance” an excited voice called from ahead of him breaking Nero from his thoughts as he looked up to see Horace riding up to the group the excitement on his face and in his movements was pouring off him, turning his horse he motioned for the three to follow him and rode on around the small bend, the soldiers along the rode looked confused, not knowing wether to stop or continue on. Nero raised a hand giving them the signal to hold and urged his horse forward following the excited Historian. Coming around the small wooded bend Nero saw the man’s horse as it stood there in the path, but there was no sign of the overweight excitable Messenger, he pulled his own animal alongside an getting down from the horse he began to canvas the surrounding woods and brush looking for any sign of the man. Nero was no tracker and soon became frustrated until the sound of rustling and branches snapping came from behind, turning her saw the large man emerge looking up Nero knew the man had truly found the entrance.

He was positively beaming as he rushed over grabbing Nero “This way, come see this my friend, you won’t believe it” he gushed practically dragging Nero along with him and into the dense woods. Nero kept his hand in front of his face as branches came snapping back as the larger Messenger plowed through the brush excitedly talking. He was far enough in front of Nero and his concentration was more on the woods then his friend that he only caught maybe every third word.

Finally Horace stopped, bringing Nero up short when he did. The Lord Regent for Vicor stepped next to the Master Historian and his eyes widened as the well hidden stone door stood before the two men. Writing adorned the large stone frame and Nero stepped closer “This treasure is one given by Aurtus to allow his chosen to combat the threat from the fallen” he whispered reading the passage carved into the stone. Nero stood there regarding the large black maw, squinting he couldn’t see beyond the entrance. Though there was no door, he couldn’t proceed without a light. Turning he found the Historian standing there holding out a small crystal lantern, Nero smiled at his friend taking the device and turning the small knob on its side.

Stepping forward he entered the order’s first holy armory, one that no Messenger had set foot in, in over four generations. The air smelled musty and despite the warm air outside, the temperature in here was cold, cold enough where he almost felt he needed a heavier coat. The red hued light dance along the narrow stone passage revealing drawings and writing covering every surface. He stopped for a moment to regard one such drawing, it was a depiction of mages, the power of fire and lightning spilling from there fingers, while the soldiers of the order marching forward, an artistic rendition of holy light surrounding them as they were protected from the power of the mages.

Well he thought, we seem to be in the right place. Turning he found his friend who had produced another light an was well back studying one of the first drawings. “My friend there will be plenty of time to study these, we must find the armory” Nero called and Horace shot him a guilty look “Of course” he said coming to stand next to the Lord Regent. They continued forward, watching the walls as drawing after drawing played out over the stone on either side of them. Suddenly the narrow passage curved left and opened up, Nero walked into the new open space, pushing the light towards the ceiling he couldn’t make it out, nor for that matter could he see the walls. He slowly moved forward the light barely cutting into the thick darkness of the cavernous area and then emerging out of the darkness a half rotted wooden clothing tree, build from wood it aloud someone to hang clothing on it draping it over the simple T the same way you would a person. Kneeling down Nero played the light over what lay on the floor, covered in a thick coating of dust, silver and bronze armor lay on the floor, the light playing over the dusty metal as he made out the lines an swirls of runic script covering the ornate armor.

Next to it lay a sword and a crossbow, both covered in the same kind of script. The string on the crossbow was long gone but the simple device as well as the long sword seemed in good condition. Behind him Horace chirped with excitement “Nero, come see” be breathed, the other man turning and walking over to the historian as he practically jumpe out of his skin. Pointing to the wall Nero saw what had him so excitable and smiled. Walking over to the wall he began to turn the large knob on the wall. He had heard of these but had never seen one. It was a room size version of the lamp he carried, as he turned the large knob, he could hear the creaking and scraping as items and cogs moved. Light began to fill the chamber and once he could turn it no longer. Nero turned to see just how big the room really was. Whistling he looked over row upon row of half rotted clothing racks and weapon racks going as far as the eye could see. Light spilled from large crystals hanging high above them, at least two stories he judged looking up at the ceiling. “How many soldiers do you think this would outfit” he asked Horace whose excitement sobered as he remembered why they were there. “I am not sure, maybe two thousand, maybe more” he said shrugging. Nero smile at the thought of two thousand trained Holy Warriors with this armor. Nero walked the rows he quickly lost count as he passed row after row of the large display room of armor. The cache that the forebears of his order had left should the agreement between mage and mundane ever be violated.

Continuing down the rows Nero came to the end of the room and stopped, staring at the back wall as a final set of armor lay on a stone bench, the armor much more ornate as was the sword and shield that sat next to it. Horace came to stand next to him and smiled “That is the armor for the Lord Regent, to the left and right is the armor for his generals and knights” he said Nero stepping forward ignoring the historian as he studied the dust covered set that was once worn by the founder and leader of the Messengers. Running his fingers over the chestplate, silver gleamed where his fingers wiped away the thick dust of time. “Call the soldiers in” he said to Horace without turning away from the set of armor. Before could Horace could turn the two hear a gasp from the entrance and turning, they found the two emissaries standing there dumbfounded. “Is this… it, is this real?” Loprin whispered walking towards the two. “It is gentlemen, and its our salvation” Nero stated.

The sun came up over the treeline the first rays played over the silver pauldrons as Nero stood there fitting the straps to the chestpiece. The night before they had moved out all of the armor and weapons, cleaning and repairing them and then as if by providence the other battalion of soldiers came into view joining the already large troop formation that Nero had. They were ready he thought, ready to finally end the Empress’s reign of terror.

“My Lord, the soldiers will be ready in an hour, they are mustering down, did you wish to speak to them?” Major Moragiven stated. He had arrived that morning with the new troops and much to the chagrin of the emissaries had presented himself first to Nero, as the new Lord Regent, he was officially in charge, but it was not until this man had bypassed the emissaries and Nero could still see the sour looks on the man’s face’s and he had to suppress a smile. Moragiven had been attentive and efficient ensuring that the troops received the armor, the repairs had been done quickly and that they were ready to go.

“I will Major, please ensure they are mustered” Nero said turning back to pick up the now gleaming long sword. Studying the long beautiful blade with its ornate runic carvings he clumsily pushed it into the sheath on his hip, the weapon was little more then an accessory at this point, he was no warrior, no General he thought. He would have to rely heavily on those around him.

“Major, I will have to rely on those around me to ensure that our plans for troops and toop movement are well planned and well executed. I will have to count on you to assist me in this” Nero said and winced, he did not like admitting his weaknesses but knew he had to. The Major looked to the Lord Regent and for a second said nothing, then with a small nod he turned and left. Nero breathed a sigh of relief, he had seen the look in the Major’s eyes, knew the man understood what he was asking and yet, he there was not distain in his eyes, he did not look down on the Lord Regent, he simply understood the need and agreed. The Major would be important to this endeavor he thought.

Nero emerged from the tent smelling the combined scent of pine and morning dew as he regarded the mass of soldiers now resplendent in the shining armor, like a sea of metal and flesh. Moragiven had setup a small podium, allowing the Lord Regent to stand above the troops. He walked up the single shaky wooden step and stood there regarding the troops as every eye in the group looked up at him. Nero took a breath, forcing down the panic as the soldiers continued to stare, continued to regard the newly minted Lord Regent of Vicor. Closing his eyes, he calmed himself, he had no words, no idea what to say to these men, these battle-hardened soldiers who now served him. “Good morning my friends, my fellow believers” he began pausing as his eyes roved over the crowd, over the sea of metal and flesh.

“Generations of ago, our leaders entered into a pact with the Mages, bringing an end to decades of war. We allowed the Mages to form their own order, gave them the ability to police themselves and to live among us, we allowed them to survive” he continued pausing as he searched the eyes looking back at him. “Now we stand here, in a land rife with the subjugation of honest hardworking people, the Mages have shown there true colors, have shown what they truly want, they believe they are better then us, they believe they should rule and in doing so they have put the yoke of slavery on people who aren’t like them” he stated, raising his voice to ensure that all could hear him.

“Now, we stand at the precipice, they have broken the agreement and it is our mandate to ensure that the ramifications of that one action are brought to bear on those who broke it” Nero could see the nodded and the whispered murmurs of agreement.

“Now we ride, we ride to remove the mages from power, we are going to take back this land and show them, we will not stand for this, we will finish what we should have finished generations ago” he finished and a cheer erupted from the crowd and Nero smiled, it was not a pleasant smile, it was a smile that promised pain.

A thrumming erupted over the morning as birds took to the air, startled and animals went to ground. The mass of soldiers five abreast marched proudly towards the capital, gleaming and ready to face the enemy that lurked there.

Loprin and Hutchin rode forward matching Nero’s speed as he rode in front of the formation, dressed in the armor of the Lord Regent that had originally hunted the Mages to near extinction. “Lord Regent, what is your plan once we reach the capital?” asked the taller Loprin. Nero was quiet, contemplating how to answer the question and finally turned to the two men.

“We will take control of Vicor, we will bring balance back to the land and then we will find a ruler, one we can trust, once we do. The Church will hand over power to them, until then we will maintain order here my friends, we will ensure that your countries are safe and ours is as well” he finished and Loprin nodded both men approving of the plan. These men had no stomach for war Nero thought they had not lived through the nightmare of what had happened in this country and only wanted to ensure the safety of their own country. Nero had bigger plans, the agreement had been broken, the mages had made their intent known, it was time to make them pay for what they had done to the people of Vicor. It was time for the time of Magic to end and Nero, at that moment commited himself to ending that age.
